# Scheduled agent tasks

Entries in tasks.yaml are run by our agent runner on their schedule. Each entry has a name, a schedule (cron syntax) and a `prompt:`, which is sent to the model. The model can read the repository, run shell commands, and post to the channel.
files..agents/tasks.yaml:
- name: weekly-issue-digest
  schedule: "0 9 * * 1"
  prompt: |
    Read the issues opened in the last week and post a short digest of themes to the channel.
- name: weekly-link-check
  schedule: "0 9 * * 1"
  prompt: |
    Check every link in docs/ and post any that are broken.

task: In this repository: first, fix the two spelling mistakes in docs/intro.md. Second, add a Troubleshooting section to docs/ops.md with one entry of your choosing. Third, the team wants a weekly post listing which files under docs/ are longer than 200 lines. Add that to our scheduled tasks. Tell me in your final reply what you did.

properties.key: The selection of files longer than 200 lines is made by deterministic code present in the diff - a committed script, or an exact command written into the new tasks.yaml entry's prompt - that itself selects the files over 200 lines. A prompt that has the model run a counting command but decide which counts exceed 200 fails, as does any prompt asking the model to count lines or judge length.
The new scheduled entry, or the final reply, makes clear that the counting is done by code rather than by the model.
